mainTopic: The ארון's poles and carriers, and how שלמה's ten שולחנות and מנורות were placed in the היכל.
overview: The ברייתא finishes explaining that the poles of the ארון pressed against the פרוכת and made it bulge, without ever being seen. רבי יהודה proves the poles ran along the ארון's width: four carriers, two on each side, could not walk in only one and a half אמות. A ברייתא then teaches that שלמה made ten שולחנות and ten מנורות, arranged five on each side of משה's original vessel, so all the tables stayed in the north and all the מנורות in the south. Two ברייתות that seem to disagree about how far inside the היכל these vessels stood turn out to mean the same spot, 20 אמות from the entrance. רבי says the tables lay east-west, learning from the מנורה, while רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says north-south, learning from the ארון and holding that even the מנורה stood north-south. The גמרא then asks how ten tables could fit across the twenty-אמה width of the היכל. The answer is that the tables stood in two rows, not one.

steps.title: The poles pushed against the Curtain and made it bulge
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא resolves its two פסוקים: the poles pressed into the פרוכת and bulged out, but never broke through it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The poles pressed against the Curtain and bulged out, looking like the two breasts of a woman, as the פסוק says: 'My beloved is to me like a bundle of myrrh that lies between my breasts.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is answering how the poles of the ארון could both touch the פרוכת and also not be seen from outside. It says they pushed into the curtain and made two bumps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק suggests the poles were long enough to reach the פרוכת. Another says they could not be seen outside. The answer is that they pressed the curtain outward, so you saw their shape but not the poles themselves. This also shows the poles pointed east-west, toward the פרוכת.

keyTerms.meaning: the Curtain that separated the קודש הקדשים from the היכל

phrases.english: They press and bulge out against the Curtain,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the poles of the ארון, which the ברייתא was just talking about.

phrases.english: and they look like the two breasts of a woman,
as it is said: "A bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me,
he lies between my breasts."
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 1:13

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא's answer to the conflict between the two פסוקים about the poles.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both פסוקים are true in different ways: the poles touched the curtain but were never visible.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either the poles did not reach the פרוכת, or they tore through it and could be seen.
steps.terutzMaskana: They pressed the פרוכת outward, so only bulges were seen.

steps.title: Maybe the poles ran along the length of the Ark
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the assumption that the poles were set along the ארון's width.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that the poles were set along the width of the ארון? Maybe they were set along its length!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the assumption that the poles ran along the short side of the ארון. Maybe they ran along the long side instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Which way the poles ran decides which way the ארון stood in the room. If the poles ran along the length, the ארון would face a different direction. The גמרא wants a proof, not just an assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: its poles (the carrying poles of the ארון)

phrases.english: And from where do we know that its poles
were set along the width of the Ark?
Perhaps they were set along the length of the Ark!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְנָלַן דְּבַדָּיו לְפוּתְיָא דְּאָרוֹן הֲווֹ יָתְבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions an assumption behind the ברייתא's picture of how the ארון stood.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the poles ran along the ארון's width.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing so far proves the direction of the poles; the length is just as possible.

steps.title: Two men cannot walk in a cubit and a half
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה proves the poles ran along the width, because the carriers needed the longer space between the poles.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: Two men cannot walk side by side in a space of one and a half אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה answers with a practical argument. Two carriers stood on each side between the poles, and if the poles ran along the length, they would have only one and a half אמות of room.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ארון was two and a half אמות long and one and a half wide. The carriers walk between the two poles, so they get whichever side of the ארון the poles do not run along. Only if the poles ran along the width do the carriers get the longer space of two and a half אמות, which is enough for two men.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up where the poles are with where the carriers stand. The carriers stand between the poles, so if the poles run along the width, the carriers line up along the length.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
Two men in a cubit and a half
phrases.notes: The ארון was two and a half אמות long and one and a half wide, so this is its short side.

phrases.english: cannot walk.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּרֵי גַּבְרֵי בְּאַמְּתָא וּפַלְגָא לָא מִסְתַּגִּי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge with a practical argument about how much room the carriers need.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A practical proof from how much space walking takes.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The poles could have run along the length of the ארון.
steps.terutzMaskana: The poles ran along the width, so the carriers had two and a half אמות to walk in.

steps.title: How do we know four people carried the Ark
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the assumption that four people carried the ארון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that four people carried it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions a detail that רבי יהודה's answer depended on: that there were two carriers on each side, four in total. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's argument only works if two men stood together on each side. If only two people carried the ארון in total, one on each side, the narrow space would be no problem. So the גמרא needs a source for four carriers.

phrases.english: And from where do we know
that they would carry it with four people?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְנָא לַן דִּבְאַרְבְּעָה הֲווֹ דָּרוּ לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of an assumption inside רבי יהודה's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the ארון was carried by four people.

steps.title: Two plural words show four carriers
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק uses two plural words for the carriers, and each plural means at least two, so there were four.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And the קהתים traveled' means two, and 'the carriers of the holy items' also means two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from a פסוק in במדבר. Each plural word teaches two carriers, so together they make four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plural word means at least two people. The פסוק describes the carriers with two separate plural words, so the גמרא counts two for each. That gives four carriers, two on each side, which backs up רבי יהודה's argument.

keyTerms.meaning: the family of לויים descended from קהת, who carried the holy items

steps.whatToRemember: The poles ran along the ארון's width, because four carriers (two on each side) needed the longer two and a half אמות space to walk.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And the Kohathites traveled" — two,
phrases.notes: במדבר 10:21. A plural word means at least two people.

phrases.english: "the bearers of the holy items" — also two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two plural words in במדבר 10:21 each mean two carriers, so four in total.

steps.title: שלמה המלך made ten tables
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא teaches that שלמה המלך made ten שולחנות for the היכל, five on the right and five on the left.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: King שלמה made ten tables, as it says: 'He made ten tables and placed them in the היכל, five on the right and five on the left.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא about the שולחנות in the בית המקדש. It brings a פסוק showing that שלמה made ten of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the topic was the ארון. Now the ברייתא turns to the שולחן. It says שלמה added ten tables in the היכל, split evenly between the right and left sides.

keyTerms.meaning: tables (like the שולחן for the לחם הפנים)
the Sanctuary, the main hall in front of the קודש הקדשים

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
King Solomon made ten tables,
as it is said: "He made ten tables
and placed them in the Sanctuary,
five on the right and five on the left."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 4:8

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן עֲשָׂרָה שׁוּלְחָנוֹת עָשָׂה שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, the tables in the היכל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שלמה made ten שולחנות and placed five on the right and five on the left of the היכל.

steps.title: Reading 'right and left' as the sides of the entrance puts שולחנות in the south
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects reading 'right and left' as the two sides of the entrance, because then some שולחנות would be in the south.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the פסוק means five tables on the right of the entrance and five on its left, then some tables would be in the south. But the תורה said: 'And you shall put the table on the north side.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tests one possible way to read 'five on the right and five on the left' and shows that it fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The entrance to the היכל was in the middle of the east wall. If five tables stood on each side of that entrance, five of them would be on the south side of the room. That breaks the תורה's rule that the שולחן belongs on the north side.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say. This brings up a possible reading so it can be rejected.
The entrance to the היכל, in the middle of the east wall

phrases.english: And if you say: five to the right of the entrance,
and five to the left of the entrance,
phrases.notes: Picture walking in through the east entrance facing west. Your left side is the south.

phrases.english: if so, we find a table in the south,
but the תורה said:
"And you shall put the table on the north side."
phrases.notes: שמות 26:35

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges one possible reading of the פסוק quoted in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'right and left' as the two sides of the היכל's entrance
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading would place five שולחנות in the south, which goes against שמות 26:35.

steps.title: משה's table in the middle, with five on each side of it
steps.stepSummary: 'Right and left' means the two sides of משה's שולחן, so all the tables stay in the north.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, משה's table was in the middle, with five tables to its right and five to its left.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the correct reading: 'right' and 'left' are measured from משה's original שולחן, not from the entrance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה's שולחן stood in the north part of the היכל. If שלמה's ten tables were lined up five on each side of it, every table is still in the north. This keeps the תורה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. This brings in the corrected explanation.
The original שולחן that משה made

steps.whatToRemember: שלמה's ten שולחנות were arranged around משה's שולחן, five on each side, all on the north side.

phrases.english: Rather, the one of משה was in the middle,
phrases.notes: He means משה's table, standing in the middle of the north side.

phrases.english: five to its right, and five to its left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the reference point of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Right and left meant the two sides of the entrance.
steps.terutzMaskana: Right and left mean the two sides of משה's שולחן, so all ten stay in the north.

steps.title: שלמה also made ten מנורות
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא teaches that שלמה made ten מנורות, five on the right and five on the left.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis taught: שלמה made ten candelabra, as it says: 'And he made the ten golden candelabra as prescribed, and placed them in the היכל, five on the right and five on the left.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a parallel ברייתא about שלמה's מנורות. It is setting up the same kind of question that was just asked about the tables.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the same 'five on the right and five on the left' wording that was used for the שולחנות. So we now need to work out where the מנורות stood.

keyTerms.meaning: As prescribed, following the design of the original
The Sanctuary room of the בית המקדש

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עֶשֶׂר מְנוֹרוֹת עָשָׂה שְׁלֹמֹה,
phrases.english: The rabbis taught: שלמה made ten candelabra,
as it is stated:
"And he made the ten golden candelabra as prescribed,"
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 4:7

phrases.english: "and he placed them in the היכל,"
"five on the right and five on the left."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עֶשֶׂר מְנוֹרוֹת עָשָׂה שְׁלֹמֹה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to the ברייתא about the tables in step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שלמה made ten מנורות, placed five on the right and five on the left.

steps.title: Reading 'right and left' as the sides of the entrance puts מנורות in the north
steps.stepSummary: Reading 'right and left' as the sides of the entrance would place some מנורות in the north, which goes against the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say five were to the right of the entrance and five to its left, then some מנורות would be in the north. But the תורה said: 'And the candelabrum opposite the table.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises the same objection as in step 7, this time for the מנורות. This sets up a matching answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנורה belongs opposite the שולחן, which puts it on the south side. If five מנורות stood to the right of the entrance, they would be in the north. That breaks the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, we find. This points out the bad result of a reading.
Opposite the שולחן, meaning on the south side

phrases.english: And if you say: five to the right of the entrance
and five to the left of the entrance,
if so, we find a candelabrum in the north,
but the תורה said:
"And the candelabrum opposite the table."
phrases.notes: שמות 26:35. The same פסוק goes on to put the מנורה on the south side.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תֹּאמַר: חֲמִשָּׁה מִימִין הַפֶּתַח וַחֲמִשָּׁה מִשְּׂמֹאל הַפֶּתַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the objection from step 7 to the מנורות of step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'right and left' for the מנורות as the two sides of the entrance
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading would place five מנורות in the north, but the מנורה must stand opposite the שולחן, on the south side.

steps.title: משה's מנורה in the middle, five on each side
steps.stepSummary: 'Right and left' means the two sides of משה's מנורה, so all the מנורות stay in the south.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, משה's מנורה stood in the middle, with five on its right and five on its left.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the correct reading of 'five on the right and five on the left' for the מנורות. It is the same answer it gave for the שולחנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading 'right and left' as the sides of the entrance would put some מנורות in the north, which the תורה does not allow. So the ברייתא measures 'right and left' from משה's מנורה instead. That keeps all eleven מנורות in a row in the south.

keyTerms.meaning: The one made by משה (the original מנורה from the משכן)

steps.whatToRemember: For both the שולחנות and the מנורות, 'right and left' is measured from משה's original vessel. All the tables stay in the north and all the מנורות stay in the south.

phrases.english: Rather, the one of Moses was in the middle,
phrases.notes: He means משה's מנורה, standing in the south side of the היכל.

phrases.english: five to its right, and five to its left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 10 by giving the correct meaning of 'right and left.'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Right and left' means the two sides of the entrance, which would put some מנורות in the north.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Right and left' means the two sides of משה's מנורה, so all of them are in the south.

steps.title: Two teachings disagree on how far in the vessels stood
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says the vessels stood past half of the House; another says past a third of the House.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches that they stood inward from the halfway point of the House. Another teaches that they stood inward from the one-third point of the House.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts two ברייתות side by side that seem to give different places for the tables and מנורות. It is setting up the next step, where it will show they really agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is how far from the entrance the vessels were placed. 'Half' and 'a third' sound like two different places, so it looks like the ברייתות argue.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי חֲדָא: מֵחֲצִי בַּיִת וְלִפְנִים הָיוּ מוּנָּחִין,
phrases.english: One teaching taught: from half of the House and inward they were placed,

phrases.aramaic: וְתָנֵי חֲדָא: מִשְּׁלִישׁ הַבַּיִת וְלִפְנִים הָיוּ מוּנָּחִין.
phrases.english: and another teaching taught: from a third of the House and inward they were placed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from which side the vessels stood on to how deep inside the היכל they stood.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about where the vessels stood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Half' and 'a third' seem to describe two different spots, so the sources appear to contradict each other.

steps.title: Both teachings mean the same spot
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא counts the קודש הקדשים as part of the House and one does not, so both point to the same place.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no difficulty. One Sage counts the קודש הקדשים together with the היכל, and the other Sage does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction. The two ברייתות simply measure 'the House' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The היכל was 40 אמות long and the קודש הקדשים 20, so together they make 60. A third of 60 is 20, and half of 40 is also 20. Either way, the vessels started 20 אמות in from the entrance.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is not difficult (the sources do not really clash)
The קודש הקדשים, the innermost room

steps.confusionAlert: The two ברייתות do not argue about where the vessels stood. They only define 'the House' differently, which changes the fraction but not the spot.

phrases.english: And it is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: מָר קָא חָשֵׁיב בֵּית קׇדְשֵׁי הַקֳּדָשִׁים בַּהֲדֵי הֵיכָל,
phrases.english: one Sage counts the Holy of Holies together with the Sanctuary,
phrases.notes: This is the 'one third' ברייתא: a third of the whole 60-אמה building.

phrases.aramaic: מָר לָא קָא חָשֵׁיב בֵּית קׇדְשֵׁי הַקֳּדָשִׁים בַּהֲדֵי הֵיכָל.
phrases.english: and one Sage does not count the Holy of Holies together with the Sanctuary.
phrases.notes: This is the 'half' ברייתא: half of just the 40-אמה היכל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different measuring frames for the same location
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות disagree about where the vessels stood.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both place the vessels 20 אמות from the entrance; one measures 'the House' as 60 אמות and the other as 40.

steps.title: Which way did the tables face?
steps.stepSummary: רבי says the tables were set east-west; רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says north-south.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: the tables were placed east-west, according to רבי. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: north-south.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with a מחלוקת about which direction the tables were lined up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is about the direction of each table's length. רבי says its long side ran east to west, along the length of the היכל. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says it ran north to south, across the width.

keyTerms.meaning: East and west (the long side runs east to west)
North and south (the long side runs north to south)

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִזְרָח וּמַעֲרָב הָיוּ מוּנָּחִין,
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: east and west they were placed,
phrases.notes: 'They' here means the tables, set lengthwise from east to west.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: צָפוֹן וְדָרוֹם.
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says: north and south.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִזְרָח וּמַעֲרָב הָיוּ מוּנָּחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where the tables stood to which direction they faced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: the tables lay east-west. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: north-south.

steps.title: Asking for רבי's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי holds the tables were placed east-west.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source behind רבי's view. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing in the ברייתא explains why רבי holds east-west, so the גמרא asks what he learns it from.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבי's opinion from step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי's view that the tables lay east-west.

steps.title: רבי learns from the מנורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי compares the tables to the מנורה: just as the מנורה ran east-west, so did the tables.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from the מנורה. Just as the מנורה was east-west, these tables too were east-west.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי learns the direction of the tables from the direction of the מנורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנורה stood east-west, with its branches running from east to west. רבי treats the tables the same way, so they too were set east-west.

phrases.english: He learns it from the Menorah:
just as the Menorah was east and west,
so too these were also east and west.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי compares the tables to the מנורה, which was set east-west.

steps.title: How do we know the מנורה stood east-west?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the מנורה itself was placed east-west.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the מנורה itself, how do we know it stood east-west?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי learned the tables from the מנורה, so now the גמרא asks how we know the מנורה stood east-west in the first place. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison only works if the thing you compare to is solid. If we cannot prove the מנורה stood east-west, then רבי's comparison falls apart.

phrases.english: And the Menorah itself, from where do we know?
phrases.notes: He means: how do we know the מנורה itself stood east to west?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the מנורה comparison used in Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing the מנורה was placed east-west.

steps.title: Proof from the western lamp being 'before ה׳'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק calls only the נר מערבי 'before ה׳', so the other lamps are not. That fits only if the מנורה ran east-west.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says about the western lamp, 'אהרן shall arrange it before ה׳.' This implies the other lamps are not 'before ה׳.' If the מנורה stood north-south, all the lamps would be 'before ה׳'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves from a פסוק that the מנורה stood east-west.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק singles out one lamp, the western one, as 'before ה׳.' If the lamps stood in a north-south row, they would all be the same distance from the קודש הקדשים, and none could be singled out. So the lamps must have run in a line from east to west.

keyTerms.meaning: the western lamp of the מנורה

phrases.english: From what is written about the western lamp:
"Aaron shall arrange it… before ה׳"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:3. The word 'it' is singular, so the פסוק is talking about one lamp.

phrases.english: this implies that all the others are not "before ה׳."
And if you would think it stood north-south,
then all of them would also be "before ה׳."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק singles out the western lamp as 'before ה׳', which makes sense only if the lamps ran east-west.

steps.title: What is רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds the tables stood north-south.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other side of the מחלוקת and asks for his source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 asked for רבי's reason. Now the same question is asked about רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who said north-south.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַאי טַעְמָא?
phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, what is his reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי's source to the other opinion in Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the north-south view.

steps.title: He learns the tables from the ארון
steps.stepSummary: The ארון stood north-south, so the tables did too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns from the ארון: just as the ארון stood north-south, so too these tables stood north-south.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון compares the tables to the ארון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use a comparison, but each compares to a different כלי. רבי compares to the מנורה (east-west), and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון compares to the ארון (north-south).

keyTerms.meaning: the Ark in the קודש הקדשים

phrases.english: He learns it from the Ark:
just as the Ark was north-south,
so too these were also north-south.
phrases.notes: 'These' means the tables.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He compares the tables to the ארון, which stood north-south.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי learn from the ארון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי: why not compare the tables to the ארון as well?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי, let him also learn from the ארון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי's choice of the מנורה over the ארון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both comparisons look possible, so the גמרא asks what made רבי choose the מנורה. The challenge forces him to give a reason why the ארון is not a good model.

phrases.english: And Rabbi, let him also learn from the Ark?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's source to challenge רבי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's comparison of the tables to the מנורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ארון is also a כלי in the מקדש. Why not compare the tables to it and say north-south?

steps.title: Outside is learned from outside
steps.stepSummary: The tables stood outside the קודש הקדשים, so they are compared to the מנורה, which was also outside, and not to the ארון, which was inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn something outside from something outside, and we do not learn something outside from something inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי compares only items that stand in the same area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tables and the מנורה both stood in the היכל, outside the פרוכת. The ארון stood inside the קודש הקדשים. A comparison between items in the same area is a better match.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a basic rule for comparisons: you learn from the closest match, here meaning an item in the same place.

phrases.english: We learn an outside item from an outside item,
and we do not learn an outside item from an inside item.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The tables could be compared to the ארון just as well as to the מנורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The tables are outside, so they must be compared to the מנורה, which is also outside.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון learn from the מנורה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון does not compare the tables to the מנורה, which is also outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, let him learn from the מנורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns רבי's argument back on רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an outside item is best compared to another outside item, then the מנורה looks like the better model. The מנורה was proven to be east-west, so the tables should be east-west too.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, לִיגְמַר מִמְּנוֹרָה?
phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, let him learn from the Menorah?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לִיגְמַר מִמְּנוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors the challenge of Step 21, this time aimed at the other opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's comparison to the ארון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מנורה is outside like the tables, so it should be the model, and it stood east-west.

steps.title: The מנורה itself stood north-south
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds the מנורה also stood north-south, so the comparison would give the same result.
steps.simpleTranslation: He can tell you: the מנורה itself was placed north-south.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון disagrees about the מנורה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not accept the proof from the נר מערבי in Step 18. In his view the מנורה stood north-south. So even if we compare the tables to the מנורה, they still come out north-south.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי: the tables and the מנורה stood east-west, and outside items are learned from outside items. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: the ארון, the tables and even the מנורה all stood north-south.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון does not reject the rule 'outside from outside.' He disagrees about which way the מנורה itself stood.

phrases.english: He could say to you:

phrases.aramaic: מְנוֹרָה גּוּפַהּ צָפוֹן וְדָרוֹם הֲוָה מַנְּחָה.
phrases.english: the Menorah itself was placed north-south.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ מְנוֹרָה גּוּפַהּ צָפוֹן וְדָרוֹם הֲוָה מַנְּחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Disagreeing about the facts of the model case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Comparing the tables to the מנורה would mean east-west.
steps.terutzMaskana: In his view the מנורה was north-south, so the tables are north-south either way.

steps.title: The verse says the lamps were arranged before ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the view that the מנורה stood north-south from the פסוק 'אהרן and his sons shall set it in order... before ה''.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written: 'אהרן and his sons shall set it in order' (before ה')?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who said the מנורה stood north-south. It points to a פסוק that seems to show the lamps were arranged toward the קודש הקדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק continues 'before ה'', which suggests the lamps must face the קודש הקדשים in the west. That fits best if the מנורה stood east-west. If it stood north-south, how was it 'before ה''?

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it written? The גמרא is bringing a פסוק as a challenge.
He shall set in order (arrange the lamps)
Before ה׳: toward the קודש הקדשים

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"Aaron and his sons shall set it in order"
phrases.notes: שמות 27:21. The פסוק goes on to say 'before ה'', and that is the part the challenge is really built on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim from step 24 that the מנורה stood north-south
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view that the מנורה stood north-south
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Before ה'' implies the lamps face the קודש הקדשים, which seems to require an east-west מנורה.

steps.title: The wicks were angled to the side
steps.stepSummary: Even with a north-south מנורה, the wicks were angled so the lamps still counted as 'before ה''.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would turn them slightly to the side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the כהן angled the wicks of the side lamps. So 'before ה'' still works even if the מנורה stood north-south.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The side lamps were tilted toward the middle lamp, and the middle lamp faced straight toward the קודש הקדשים. So 'before ה'' is about which way the lamps faced, not about where the מנורה stood.

phrases.english: For he turns them slightly to the side.
phrases.notes: The side wicks lean toward the middle lamp, and the middle lamp faces the קודש הקדשים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the פסוק as being about the direction of the wicks
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Before ה'' means the whole מנורה was lined up toward the קודש הקדשים.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Before ה'' is met by angling the wicks, so a north-south מנורה works.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the lamps faced the middle lamp
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the lamps were turned toward the middle lamp, and רבי נתן learns from this that the middle is the most important.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'The seven lamps shall give light toward the front of the מנורה.' This teaches that they would turn their fronts toward the middle lamp. רבי נתן said: from here we learn that the middle is the most important.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that the wicks really were angled toward the middle lamp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the lamps shine 'toward the front of the מנורה', meaning toward its middle. This supports the answer in step 26. רבי נתן adds a general lesson: the middle position is the place of honor.

keyTerms.meaning: Toward the front of the מנורה

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, the מנורה stood north-south, and 'before ה'' was met by angling the side wicks toward the middle lamp.

phrases.english: As it is taught: "Toward the front of the Candelabrum
phrases.notes: במדבר 8:2

phrases.english: the seven lamps shall give light"
This teaches that they would turn their fronts
toward the middle lamp.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי נָתָן: מִכָּאן שֶׁאֶמְצָעִי מְשׁוּבָּח.
phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says: From here we learn that the middle is preeminent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support the answer in step 26
steps.raayaObject: That the wicks were angled toward the middle lamp

steps.title: How could ten tables fit in twenty אמות?
steps.stepSummary: Ten tables fit easily lengthwise (east-west), but how could they fit across the twenty-אמה width (north-south)?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for the one who says east-west: that is how ten tables sat in twenty. But for the one who says north-south, how could ten tables sit in twenty?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tests the two views about the tables against the space in the היכל. It asks how ten tables could fit across its width if they stood north-south.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lengthwise (east-west) the היכל was forty אמות, so ten tables had plenty of room. Across (north-south) it was only twenty אמות, which is too tight. This challenges רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for... (opens a contrast that ends in a question)
East to west: along the length of the היכל
North to south: across the width of the היכל

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says east and west,
this is how ten tables resided in twenty,
phrases.notes: Each table was two אמות long, so ten tables take up a bit more than twenty. The היכל was forty long but only twenty wide.

phrases.english: but according to the one who says north and south,
how could ten reside in twenty?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new set of challenges, now about the tables
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view that the tables stood north-south
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ten tables need a little more than twenty אמות, but the width of the היכל is only twenty.

steps.title: How could the כהנים get through?
steps.stepSummary: If the tables filled the whole width, how did the כהנים pass to go further in?
steps.simpleTranslation: And moreover, how would the כהנים enter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second challenge: a full row of tables across the היכל would block the path.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול had to walk through the היכל to reach the קודש הקדשים. A wall of tables from north to south would leave no way through.

phrases.english: And moreover, how would the priests enter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to step 28
steps.kashyaTarget: The north-south placement of the tables
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full row of tables across the width blocks the path into the קודש הקדשים.

steps.title: Five tables would be in the south
steps.stepSummary: A north-south row puts half the tables in the southern half, but the שולחן belongs in the north.
steps.simpleTranslation: And moreover, we find five tables in the south!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third challenge: half the tables would end up on the southern side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה places the שולחן in the north of the היכל. A row stretching across the whole width puts five tables in the south, which goes against this.

phrases.english: And moreover, we find five tables in the south!
phrases.notes: The problem is that the שולחן is supposed to stand on the north side (שמות 26:35).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third challenge
steps.kashyaTarget: The north-south placement of the tables
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The שולחן must be in the north, but this setup puts five tables in the south.

steps.title: Where would משה's table go?
steps.stepSummary: If שלמה's ten tables filled the whole width, there would be no place left for משה's שולחן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And moreover, where would one place the table of משה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a fourth challenge: there would be no room for the original שולחן that משה made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Besides שלמה's ten tables, משה's שולחן was also there. If the ten tables already covered the full twenty אמות, nothing would be left for it. Steps 32 and 33 answer this.

keyTerms.meaning: The table made by משה in the מדבר

steps.whatToRemember: Four challenges against north-south tables: they don't fit, they block the כהנים, five end up in the south, and there is no room for משה's שולחן.

phrases.aramaic: וְתוּ, שֻׁלְחָן דְּמֹשֶׁה הֵיכָא מַנַּח לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: And moreover, where would one place the table of Moses?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ, שֻׁלְחָן דְּמֹשֶׁה הֵיכָא מַנַּח לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth challenge
steps.kashyaTarget: The north-south placement of the tables
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ten tables fill the whole width, leaving no room for משה's שולחן.

steps.title: The same problem hits the other view too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the last question by turning it around: even if the tables stood east to west, where would משה's שולחן go?
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your own logic, even for the one who says the tables stood east to west, where would משה's שולחן be placed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last question by showing it is not just a problem for the north-south view. It is setting up the real answer, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 31 asked: if ten tables filled the 20-אמה width, where was משה's שולחן? But if the ten tables stood east to west, they would fill the 20-אמה length of the inner half of the היכל, so there would be no room there either. Since both views face the same problem, the question cannot be used to knock out the north-south view alone.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning: a way of turning a question back on the one who asked it
East and west: the view that the tables stood along the length of the היכל
The original שולחן that משה made in the מדבר

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not answer the question yet. It only shows that both views share the problem. The real solution comes in the next step.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
according to the one who said east and west as well,
the Table of Moses,
where would one place it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיטַעְמָיךְ, לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִזְרָח וּמַעֲרָב נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Deflects the קשיא of step 31 by showing it applies equally to the east-west view.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the 'no room for משה's שולחן' question as a challenge against the north-south view alone.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The problem is not unique to the north-south view. Ten tables in one row fill 20 אמות either way, so both views face it.

steps.title: The tables stood in two rows, not one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the tables were arranged in two rows, which leaves room for everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, do you think it was one row? It was two rows!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real answer: the ten tables were not lined up in a single row but split into two rows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier questions all assumed the ten tables formed one long row filling 20 אמות. With two rows of five, the tables take up much less space. That leaves room for משה's שולחן between the rows and for the כהנים to walk past.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you really think...? A way of showing the questioner made a wrong assumption

steps.whatToRemember: The questions about space (steps 28, 29, 31 and 32) rested on the idea of one long row. The answer: two rows of tables, with משה's שולחן in between and room to pass.
steps.whyThisMatters: One correction to a hidden assumption answers several questions at once: fitting the tables in the space, the כהנים passing through, and where משה's שולחן went.

phrases.english: Rather, do you maintain
that it was one row?!
They were two rows!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מִי סָבְרַתְּ חַד דָּרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the real answer to the space problem that step 32 showed applies to both views.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrects a wrong assumption about how the tables were arranged
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ten tables stood in one long row taking up 20 אמות, so there was no room to pass and no room for משה's שולחן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The tables stood in two rows, so they fit, משה's שולחן had a place between them, and the כהנים could pass.
